problem: Zero-shot semantic maps for VLN are either 2D (collapse vertical structure, blend stacked objects, lose small objects) or 3D scene graphs like HOV-SG (storage-heavy, SAM+CLIP over-segmentation). Keyword-based query processing discards descriptive content and cannot handle abstract queries.
motivation: Reliable indoor navigation needs instance-level detail, attribute/room context and robustness to diverse query phrasing, while remaining storage-efficient for long-term deployment. A single LLM pass over all instance info conflates the different information dimensions of queries.
key_idea: Build a compact instance-level 2.5D map (multiple instance indices per grid cell) enriched with room labels and VLM captions, and select goals with a gate LLM that weights type-specialized expert LLMs whose rankings are fused at score level.
insight: Giving HOV-SG the same captions (w/ desc.) yields only marginal gains (O-SR e.g. 8→10 on (o,r,d)), showing richer stored info alone is insufficient and the MTEFR routing/fusion is the main driver. Full+MTEFR beats the single-pass LLM variant (70 vs 58 O-SR on (o); 14 vs 6 on (a,r,d)). SEEM panoptic masks plus object-level storage sharply reduce spurious instances (Instance Diff 2.6 vs 86.6 on Replica) and storage (10 MB vs 248 MB).
method: Instance-level 2.5D mapping: SEEM panoptic masks+embeddings from RGB-D projected top-down; association via max-overlap geometric and cosine semantic similarity (convex combination); weighted feature fusion; second global association pass merges duplicates; each cell stores a list of instance indices
Open-vocabulary instance categorization: argmax similarity between instance embeddings and SEEM text embeddings of a category list
Room-level segmentation: structural masks (walls, doors) -> LSD line detection with NFA filter -> connected components as room instances; dense CLIP pixel labels aggregated by majority vote per room
Instance captioning: LLaMA 3.2 Vision describes keyframes (color, material, texture, shape); GPT-4 condenses into compact caption plus key-value tags; room tag attached
Obstacle map: height threshold plus open-vocabulary obstacle categories from the 2.5D map
MTEFR: gate LLM outputs weights over obj/room/desc/abs expert LLMs; each expert ranks top-κ candidates (κ=2); rank scores fused as λ·peak + (1-λ)·weighted sum with λ schedule (γ=0.75, μ=16)

setting.backbone: SEEM (Focal-L), CLIP, LLaMA 3.2 Vision, GPT-4 (gate/expert/caption LLMs), all frozen
setting.observation: RGB-D with camera poses (from simulator/SLAM), pre-exploration to build map
setting.action_space: navigation to goal location on map (path planning on obstacle map); not learned low-level actions
setting.privileged: GT camera poses; map built from a prior exploration phase; single-floor assumption

numbers.eval_set_note: 5 HM3DSEM scenes, first floor, 50 trials per query type per scene (250 trials per type), 30 most frequent categories
numbers.extra: pre-built map; N-SR conditional on retrieval success; success within 1 m

numbers_note: Custom benchmark (not standard VLN); per-query-type entries. Mapping metrics (AUC, mIoU, storage) are in other tables and not listed.
results: The 2.5D map improves prediction-normalized AUC over HOV-SG (0.356 vs 0.093 Replica; 0.371 vs 0.085 HM3DSEM), room segmentation mIoU rises 0.53→0.75 over CLIP, and storage is 10 MB vs 248 MB (HOV-SG). In navigation, MTEFR beats HOV-SG in O-SR on all query types (e.g. 70 vs 40 on (o), 14 vs 2 on (a,r,d)), with roughly 17% average O-SR and 23% N-SR gains.
limitations: Multiple VLMs/LLMs cause computational overhead, preventing real-time use; only simulation, no real-robot test
Room segmentation relies on physical partitions and fails in open-plan areas; single-floor assumption
Abstract queries with broad semantic interpretations remain hard (14% O-SR); captions can be wrong from limited viewpoints; evaluated on small custom query set
